# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)</sub>
- **Titles:** queen of housemothers  <sub>[v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>; Aunty J.  <sub>[v3 c24 P5](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny old woman with a softly-triangular face, pink cheeks, and large, soft blue eyes filled with youth and hope. She has snow-white hair worn in quaint little puffs over her ears. She dresses in old-fashioned clothes.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina is sweet, cheerful, and holds quaint, old-fashioned views while remaining indulgent and easygoing. She possesses mirthful, twinkling young eyes and a philosophy of doing her duty while having a good time. She is deeply affectionate toward the girls she housemothers, even when she finds their behavior baffling. Though respectful of the clergy, she harbors a playful side, admitting she used to make fun of her suitors.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c18 P2](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0002), [v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004), [v3 c19 P40](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0040), [v3 c24 P5](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0005), [v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021), [v3 c37 P42](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0042)_

## History

Aunt Jamesina was named after her father James, who drowned at sea a month before she was born. After her daughter Elizabeth married and moved to India as a foreign missionary, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house. To alleviate her loneliness, she moved to Kingsport to keep house at Patty's Place for college students Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon, bringing along her sleek gray-and-white cat, the Sarah-cat. During her time as housemother, she looked after the girls with easygoing indulgence, cared for the household cats, and warmly welcomed their visitors. She developed a strong affection for the household and took a great liking to Roy Gardner, considering him a fine young man for Anne. After the girls finished their studies, Aunt Jamesina took the pets home with her. Despite a long-standing horror of snakes, she later traveled to India to explore her daughter's mission field.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c26 P18](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0018), [v3 c37 P12](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0012), [v3 c38 P8](../source/v03-c38.md#nw-v03-c38-p0008), [v4 c3 P16](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0016)_

## Background by volume

- named after her father who drowned before her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- never allowed by her mother or husband to have a yellow silk dress  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>
- given a cat named Sarah by her washerwoman  <sub>[v3 c16 P58](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0058)</sub>
- used to make fun of her suitors  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>
- suggested a rubber band ear-training method to a suitor  <sub>[v3 c37 P40](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0040)</sub>
- taught her daughter Elizabeth to cook before college  <sub>[v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006)</sub>
- prayed that her daughter would become a missionary  <sub>[v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>

## Quotes

> It’s a very old-fashioned way, but I am old-fashioned. My clothes are, and it stands to reason my opinions are, too.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> Do your duty by God and your neighbor and yourself, and have a good time. That’s my philosophy and it’s always worked pretty well.  <sub>[v3 c19 P4](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0004)</sub>

> The very first thing I’m going to do when I get to heaven is to get a yellow silk dress.  <sub>[v3 c19 P6](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0006)</sub>

> I am not decrying the higher education of women. My daughter is an M.A. She can cook, too. But I taught her to cook before I let a college professor teach her Mathematics.  <sub>[v3 c27 P6](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0006)</sub>

> It isn’t in good taste to make fun of your beaux, but I always did it myself.  <sub>[v3 c35 P21](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0021)</sub>
